title: Cinnamon rolls
description: Soft rolls with a flour–milk starter, brown butter filling, and cream cheese frosting.
equipment: Stand mixer with dough hook, {{pans}} {{pan-label}}, rolling pin, serrated knife or unflavored dental floss.

ingredients.name: unsalted butter, room temperature, cut into pieces
unsalted butter, room temperature, plus more for pans
All-purpose flour, for the work surface

steps.title: Cook the flour–milk starter
steps.text:
Whisk {{starter-milk}} whole milk and {{starter-flour}} ({{starter-flour-g}}) all-purpose flour in a medium saucepan until smooth.

Place over medium heat and cook, whisking constantly, until the mixture thickens and whisk lines are visible on the bottom of the pan, about 2 minutes.

Scrape this starter (tangzhong) into the bowl of a stand mixer and let cool.

steps.title: Mix and knead
steps.text:
To the cooled starter, add {{egg}}, {{yeast}} ({{yeast-oz}} ; about {{yeast-tsp}}) instant yeast, {{sugar}} ({{sugar-g}}) granulated sugar, {{salt}} kosher salt, and the remaining {{remaining-milk}} whole milk. Whisk to combine.

Add the remaining {{remaining-flour}} ({{remaining-flour-g}}) all-purpose flour. Fit the mixer with its dough hook. Mix on low until combined, about 1 minute.

Increase to medium-low. Mix, occasionally scraping down the bowl, until smooth and elastic, 18–24 minutes.

Check the dough: Pinch off a golf-ball-size piece and stretch it between your fingers as thinly as possible without breaking. If light shows through, it is ready. Otherwise, mix a few minutes longer and test again.

steps.title: Add butter and let rise
steps.text:
Add {{dough-butter}} ({{dough-butter-stick}}) room-temperature unsalted butter, cut into pieces. Mix on medium until incorporated, about 2 minutes.

Continue mixing until the dough pulls cleanly away from the bowl and is no longer tacky, 5–7 minutes longer.

Remove the bowl from the mixer and cover with a damp kitchen towel. Leave in a warm spot until doubled in volume, 60–90 minutes.

steps.title: Brown the butter and mix
steps.text:
While the dough rises, cook {{filling-butter}} ({{filling-butter-stick}}) unsalted butter in a small saucepan over medium heat, stirring occasionally. When it foams and the milk solids turn dark amber, about 4 minutes, transfer it to a heatproof bowl. Let cool slightly.

Mix in {{brown-sugar}} ({{brown-sugar-g}}) dark brown sugar, {{cinnamon}} ground cinnamon, {{filling-cream}} heavy cream, and {{filling-salt}} kosher salt.

steps.title: Roll out and fill
steps.text:
Butter {{pans}} {{pan-label}}. Punch down the dough and move it to a lightly floured surface. Divide into {{portions}} {{portion-label}} and shape each portion separately.

Stretch into a rough rectangle. If stiff, let it rest 5–10 minutes so the gluten can relax.

Roll each portion into a {{width}} × 13-inch rectangle, with the {{width}}-inch edge closest to you. Divide the filling evenly among the portions and spread it over each rectangle.

steps.title: Shape the rolls and let rise
steps.text:
Starting at the edge closest to you, roll the dough tightly into a log. Turn it seam-side down.

With a sharp serrated knife and long sawing motions, trim and discard the ends. Cut each log into roughly 2-inch-wide rounds, using the serrated knife or, preferably, unflavored dental floss. Aim for about {{rolls}} rolls total.

Using floss: Slide it underneath the dough, cross it over the top, and pull the ends through.

Arrange the rolls cut-side down, with up to 6 rolls per pan. Cover with damp kitchen towels and leave in a warm spot until doubled in volume, about 30–50 minutes.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text:
Position a rack in the middle of the oven and preheat to 350°F.

Bake until the rolls are golden on top and puffed, 25–30 minutes. A dramatic rise in the center is normal.

steps.title: Make the frosting
steps.text:
Meanwhile, beat {{frosting-butter}} room-temperature unsalted butter and {{cream-cheese}} room-temperature cream cheese in a large bowl with an electric mixer on medium speed or a whisk. Scrape down the bowl as needed and beat until combined.

Add {{powdered-sugar}} ({{powdered-sugar-g}}) powdered sugar, {{frosting-cream}} heavy cream, {{lemon-zest}} lemon zest (optional), and {{frosting-salt}} kosher salt. Beat until smooth and the sugar is incorporated.

Taste and beat in up to {{extra-powdered-sugar}} additional powdered sugar, if desired. Thin with more cream, 1 teaspoon at a time, until thick but spreadable.

steps.title: Cool briefly and frost
steps.text: Let the cinnamon rolls cool in their pans for 5 minutes, then spread the frosting over them.
